lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Apply a four-item checklist to: "we was late for the ferry?"

FEEDBACK
We were late for the ferry. Capital; were; full stop or keep ? only if it is a question.

CHECK
Editing before revising can polish a broken plot; do meaning first.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Create a personal eight-item editing checklist. Apply it to a 150-word draft, record six fixes and explain which two errors you miss most often.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Create a personal eight-item editing checklist. Apply it to a 150-word draft, record six fixes and explain which two errors you miss most often. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: We were late for the ferry. Capital; were; full stop or keep ? only if it is a question. Reasoning: I used editing by attending to checklist rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Editing before revising can polish a broken plot; do meaning first. Correction: We were late for the ferry. Capital; were; full stop or keep ? only if it is a question. Why: the correction restores accurate use of editing.

Parent: Likely misconception: Editing before revising can polish a broken plot; do meaning first. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating editing on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with editing, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Require independently produced work with a specific supporting detail. / Require misconception + correction + purpose-linked reason..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Checklist pass on "mia run to the Gate she dont see the sign": Mia ran to the gate. She doesn’t see the sign. (Or past: didn’t.) Capitals, tense/agreement, end marks.

TRY FIRST
Apply a four-item checklist to: "we was late for the ferry?"

FEEDBACK
We were late for the ferry. Capital; were; full stop or keep ? only if it is a question.
teach_steps.explain:
An editing checklist catches capitals, end marks, common spellings and agreement after meaning revisions are done.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
teach_steps.notice: Editing before revising can polish a broken plot; do meaning first. Correct the meaning, not just the appearance.
